newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks weaker in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks weaker in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were weaker on Friday morning but off a sharp 100-point opening drop on futures-linked trade and Wall Street's weakness, brokers said.

"The market is quite resilient," said the head of trading at an international brokerage house. "It is coming back after a sharp markdown in HSBC at the open, probably (due to) arbitrage linked trading."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 63 points down at 12,410.88 after 30 minutes of trade on Wednesday morning, off a low of 12,363.72. Trading activity was brisk with turnover rising to HK$1.17 billion.
"The arbitrage trading is very short term, the trader said.
The Hang Seng Index October futures contract was trading at 12,380, down 84 points in moderately active trade of 3,057 contracts.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 44 points to 5,992, its fourth consecutive loss and the one that brought it below the key psychological level of 6,000 for the first time in two weeks.
"The Hong Kong market also has been able to take advantage of the weakness in the Thai, Philippines and Singapore markets, but we may see a reversal of that trend now," said the trader.
Hong Kong has had a huge outperformance compared to other Southeast Asian markets and investors may want to reposition themselves in Singapore and Thailand, brokers said.
"Hong Kong's outperformance is close to ending," said Chris Sawtell, director technical strategy at W.I.Carr.
Technical indicators suggest that the market is likely to weather this pullback, but any further weakness would be a sign for caution, he said.
"If the Hang Seng holds above 12,400 today (at the close), the market will rally back up through 12,500 and then has a chance at 13,000, said Sawtell.
The finance sector led the index down, followed by utilities.
HSBC was marked down 1.2 percent at the open, to HK$155.50 from its Thursday close of HK$158.00, said the trader.
Hang Seng Bank also was trading down HK$0.75 at HK$91.50 after opening weaker at HK$90.50.

Trading in Hopewell subsidiary Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) was active following news of a potential offer for CEPA from YTL of Malaysia. CEPA and Hopewell were unchanged at HK$17.95 and HK$5.35.
